title: Dave Dexter's book misreports Mildred's remark about Billie
summary: A phrase in a book made it seem Mildred hated Billie, whereas she meant 'this kid can really sing' as the biggest compliment.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: But I picked up a guy -- newspaperman had a book, said, I got a book here, Dave Dexter wrote. Now if
you know in the old days, used to turn words around --
Yeah.
Right?
Yes.
And Mildred was a champion of that.
Yeah, yeah.

Well he would repeat -- repeated a phrase in that book, that made it appear like Mildred detested Billie and hated her because she sang better than Mildred. Which I'm sure never entered Billie's or Mildred's mind at all.
No.

And I was very put out at Dave, I've known him for years and we knew him in Kansas City, but just by the inflex of what she said, like -- well say it right, she said, this kid can really sing, dammit, or something like that --
Yeah.
-- you know she could really -- and you could say it that way and --
And it's the biggest compliment there is.
That's right.
And he would report it so that --
And you can say that in a lot of different context and -- and it the way it was in the book this writer got entirely different thing like -- oh, there was bad blood and all this sort of thing --
Yes, yes.
-- and it wasn't -- she was envious, wasn't so at all.
No. No.
I know you knew her, you knew that she wasn't envious -
